headline: Visit England's rolling hills and International Dark Sky Reserve
reservation: Access to the park is generally free and open, but accommodation in historic market towns often fills quickly. While entry permits are not typically required for individuals, large groups or those using specific historic estate facilities should verify access requirements. The park is highly accessible with many local rail connections, but always check the official South Downs National Park Authority website for the most recent policy changes.

days.title: Chalk Cliffs and Coastline

stops.name: Beachy Head
stops.detail: Visit the highest chalk sea cliff in Britain for expansive views of the Sussex Heritage Coast and the Belle Tout Lighthouse.

stops.name: Seven Sisters
stops.detail: Walk the iconic rippling wall of chalk cliffs, formed by ancient dry valleys now eroded by the sea.

days.driving: Allow 1-2 hours; conditions vary by coastal traffic
days.note: Walking the cliff edges requires caution due to natural erosion processes.

days.title: Historic Estates and Ancient Yews

stops.name: Arundel Castle
stops.detail: Explore this restored medieval castle situated in the heart of the National Park's diverse landscape.

stops.name: Kingley Vale
stops.detail: Discover ancient yew woodlands with trees estimated to be over 2,000 years old on steep hangar slopes.

days.driving: Allow 1.5-2 hours; conditions vary on rural lanes
days.note: Ancient woodlands are delicate habitats; please stay on established paths.

days.title: Dark Skies and High Points

stops.name: Black Down
stops.detail: Climb to the park's highest point at 280m for panoramic views across the Weald and wooded sandstone hills.

stops.name: Woolmer Forest
stops.detail: Visit a vital heathland haven known for supporting all 12 of Britain's native reptile and amphibian species.

days.driving: Allow 1 hour; conditions vary near market towns
days.note: As a Dark Sky Reserve, stargazing is best planned for clear nights away from town centers.

intel.title: Public Transport
intel.text: The park is incredibly accessible by rail, with several stations located near key trailheads and historic villages. Visitors are encouraged to use these links to reduce road congestion and soak up the views.

intel.title: Gateway Supplies
intel.text: Fuel and electric charging are widely available in gateway towns like Winchester, Petersfield, and Lewes. Once deep in the western Weald, service stations are less frequent.

intel.title: Village Parking
intel.text: Parking in hidden villages and near popular spots like Seven Sisters is often limited. Arriving early or using local bus transfers is suggested during peak summer periods.

intel.title: Rural Coverage
intel.text: Cellular signals are reliable in most market towns but can be intermittent in deep ancient woodlands and steep hangar valleys. Offline maps are useful for the 160km South Downs Way.

intel.title: Seasonal Wildlife
intel.text: Summer is the best time to see up to 30 butterfly species on the chalk grasslands. Heathlands transform into a sea of pink and purple during the late summer flowering period.

plan.arrival: First two hours: Pickup rental in London or Winchester, stock up in Winchester's market center, and head toward the western Weald trails.
plan.vehicle: Standard cars are ideal for narrow ancient lanes; check rental agreements for restrictions on unpaved byways.
plan.goldenHour: Lord's Piece Common offers spectacular sunrise views, though light varies seasonally over the heathland.
